q: 1. The diagram showing the variation of axial load along the span is called
explain: A thrust diagram specifically plots the variation of axial (normal) force/thrust along the length of a member, as distinct from shear force or bending moment diagrams.

q: 2. In a pin jointed frame, the members meeting at a joint must be so arranged that
options: the axes of all the members are concurrent and co planar
not more than two axes meet at a point
the axes must be parallel to each other
at least three axes meet at a common point
explain: For a pin joint to be in proper equilibrium without unintended moments, all member axes meeting there must be concurrent (intersect at one point) and lie in the same plane.

q: 3. A tie is a member which
options: a subjected to axial tensional primarily
does not suffer any stress irrespective of loading conditions
explain: A tie is defined as a structural member that is primarily subjected to axial tensile force.

q: 4. The number of reaction components possible at a hinged end for a general loading is
explain: A hinged (pinned) support prevents translation in both horizontal and vertical directions, resulting in two reaction components, but it does not resist rotation.

q: 5. A body is said to be in equilibrium if
explain: True equilibrium requires zero net force and zero net moment; a body moving or rotating is not in static equilibrium, so 'none of these' correctly excludes all listed motions.

q: 6. In any determinate structure, vertical load fall on the
explain: Determinate structures can have various support types (hinges, rollers) that receive and transfer vertical loads to the foundation.

q: 7. The maximum tension in a cable occurs
options: at the highest point in the cable
at the lowest point in the cable
at the centre point of the cable
at all points in the cable
explain: Tension is the vector sum of horizontal thrust and vertical shear; since vertical shear is highest at the supports (highest points), the tension is maximum there.

q: 8. A fixed support for a space structure
options: permits the translation only in all directions
permits rotation only about all three mutually perpendicular axes through the joint
permits rotation about all three mutually perpendicular axes and movement in any direction in the plane of the base
permits neither rotation about nor translation along, any of the three principal axes
explain: A fixed support provides total restraint, preventing both translation and rotation in all three dimensions.

q: 9. Free body diagram is
options: the diagram of the body or a part of the body in isolated equilibrium
the diagram of a body freed from all the forces that have been acting
the diagram of a body with no supports at all
explain: A Free Body Diagram (FBD) isolates a body or segment to show all active forces and reactive components acting on it.

q: 10. The free body diagram of a portion of a body will be in equilibrium under the action of
options: only external loading acting on that part without consideration of support reactions
all super-imposed loads, self-weight, support reactions, if any, and the internal reactions exposed at the cuts
only support reactions and the internal reactions exposed at the cuts
external loading acting on that part and internal reactions exposed at the cuts
explain: For any portion of a structure to be in equilibrium, all forces (external, gravity, and internal forces at the cut section) must be accounted for.

q: 11. The design of a structure is
options: the calculation of straining actions at salient points
deciding the material and proportions of the various members of the structure
explain: Design involves selecting materials and determining member sizes to ensure the structure can safely resist the analyzed forces.

q: 12. In a pin jointed plane frame all the loads are assumed to act
options: in the plane of the frame
perpendicular to the plane of the frame
in a plane inclined at 45 degrees to the plane of the frame
explain: In the analysis of plane trusses, it is a fundamental assumption that all applied loads and reactions act within the plane of the structure.

q: 13. A pin jointed frame with with J number of joints and n, number of members will be a perfect frame if
explain: A perfect (just-rigid) plane frame satisfies the condition $$n = 2j - 3$$, where it is stable and determinate.

q: 14. Find the no of joint in a structure if the number of member is 3 for a determinate structure.
explain: For a determinate truss, m = 2j - 3. If m = 3, then 3 = 2j - 3, which leads to 2j = 6, so j = 3.

q: 15. For finding forces in the members of a truss by the graphical method. The force diagram is suggested by
explain: The Maxwell-Cremona diagram is a well-known graphical method used to determine the internal forces in the members of a static truss.

q: 16. Degree of freedom (DOF) or DKI, for the structure is
explain: Based on the standard analysis of the joint configuration shown in typical structural problems of this level, the kinematic indeterminacy (DKI) refers to the independent displacement components; for the specific frame provided in the image, the answer is 2.

q: 17. In a co planar parallel force system, the number of unknown forces that can be found by the principle of statics is
explain: A coplanar parallel force system has only 2 independent equilibrium equations available (ΣF=0 along the force direction, and ΣM=0), since ΣF perpendicular to forces is automatically satisfied.

q: 18. Force is the product of
explain: According to Newton's Second Law, $F = m \cdot a$.

q: 19. The effective length of a column with one end fixed and the other end free is
explain: For a column fixed at one end and free at the other, the effective length is Le = 2L.

q: 20. Which of the following is a true example of a statically determinate beam?
options: one end is fixed and the other end is simply supported
the beam over hangs over two support
the beam is supported on three supports
explain: An overhanging beam with two supports has three reaction components, which can be solved with three equilibrium equations.

q: 21. A plane structure when subjected to a force lying outside the plane will be
explain: A plane structure is designed to resist in-plane forces; a force acting out of its plane (out-of-plane) causes instability since it cannot properly resist such loading.

q: 22. A three hinged arch is generally hinged at its supports and
explain: A three-hinged arch has hinges at both supports (springing) plus a third hinge typically placed at the crown (highest point) for symmetry and constructional convenience.

q: 23. The ordinates of influence line diagram for bending moment always has the dimensions of
explain: An influence line for bending moment plots the moment produced at a section per unit load moving across the span; since moment = force×length, per unit force this ratio has dimensions of length.

q: 24. Principle of superposition is applicable when
options: deflections are linear functions of applied forces
the action of applied forces will be affected by small deformations of the structure
explain: The principle of superposition holds when the structural response (deflections, forces) is a linear function of the applied loads — the fundamental condition for combining effects of multiple loads.

q: 25. The line of thrust of the linear arch is
options: the imaginary link work of thrust for a given set of loads
explain: The line of thrust represents the locus of resultant force (like an imaginary funicular/linkwork polygon) for a given set of loads on the arch.

q: 26. The maximum bending moment due to a train of wheel loads on a simply supported girder .............
options: always occurs at the center of span
always occurs under a wheel load
never occurs under a wheel load
explain: For moving wheel loads on a simply supported girder, the absolute maximum bending moment always occurs directly under one of the wheel loads (specifically under the load nearest the resultant of the load system), not necessarily at midspan.

q: 27. For analyzing pin jointed frames by method of joints, the joints must be selected in succession such that
options: only two members meet at that joint
only three members meet at that joint
only two unknown forces exist at that point
there is no external forces acting in the joint
explain: The method of joints requires proceeding to joints where only 2 unknown member forces remain, since only 2 equilibrium equations are available per joint to solve them.

q: 28. A support over which the real beam is continuous will correspond to .............
options: an internal hinge in the conjugate beam
a hinged support in the conjugate beam
a fixed support in the conjugate beam
a discontinuity in the conjugate beam
explain: A continuous support in the real beam (where slope is continuous but moment may be nonzero) corresponds to an internal hinge in the conjugate beam.

q: 29. The displacements of a truss can be obtained directly from
explain: The Williot-Mohr diagram is a specific graphical method used to directly determine joint displacements of a truss.

q: 30. The basic form of a pin jointed frame is
explain: A triangle is the only basic polygon shape that is inherently rigid (stable) when pin-jointed, making it the fundamental unit of truss construction.

q: 31. In a pin jointed plane frame, all the loads will be assumed to act at .............
options: only on the top chords joints
explain: For a truss to be analyzed with members carrying only axial forces, loads must be idealized as acting only at the joints (pins), not along member lengths.

q: 32. The effect of arching a beam is
explain: By 'arching' a beam (curving it to more closely follow the funicular/thrust line for the given loads), bending moment throughout the member is reduced compared to a straight beam.

q: 33. Due to rise in temperature, in a three hinged arch, induced stress is
explain: Because a three-hinged arch is statically determinate, a temperature change causes free thermal expansion/contraction (accommodated by hinge rotations) without inducing any internal stress.

q: 34. A linear arch has
explain: This item appears to reference the shape of the linear arch's constituent link-work (a triangle being the basic funicular polygon shape), matching option (a) per the source's answer key.

q: 35. A linear arch has
explain: A linear (funicular) arch, by definition, follows exactly the thrust line for its loading, so it develops only normal (axial) thrust, with zero shear and bending moment.

q: 36. A truss containing j joints and m members, will be a simple truss if
explain: The standard condition for a statically determinate (simple) truss relates members and joints as m = 2j − 3 (accounting for 3 reaction components).

q: 37. A compound truss may be formed by connecting two simple rigid frames by
options: three bars intersecting at a point
explain: Two simple rigid (stable) truss units can be combined into a stable compound truss by connecting them with exactly three non-parallel, non-concurrent bars.

q: 38. The forces in the members of simple trusses, may be analysed by
explain: Truss member forces can be determined by any of the graphical method, method of joints, or method of sections — all are valid standard techniques.

q: 39. If two force acting at a joint are not along the straight line, then for the equilibrium of the joint
options: one of the forces must be zero
forces must be equal and of the same sign
forces must be equal in magnitude but opposite in sign
explain: If two non-collinear forces act at a joint with no other forces, equilibrium (ΣF=0 in two independent directions) can only be satisfied if both forces are individually zero.

q: 40. A member is balanced at its end by two inclined members carrying equal forces, equilibrium the angle between the inclined bars must be
explain: For two equal-force inclined members to balance a load symmetrically at a joint with no other member, the resultant condition for equilibrium requires the two members to be at 120° to each other (each at 60° to the load line).
